messages:
maria: Heads-up — tracking a few upstream moves that could change our kernel selection heuristics. FlashAttention repo just merged a default block-size tweak (https://github.com/flash-attn/flash-attn/pull/987). Quick local run on A100 (8k seq) shows ~5% latency win but ~+8% peak memory for very long seqs. Command I used:
```
git fetch origin pull/987/head:pr-987
python bench_attn.py --model gpt2 --seq 8192 --kernel flash2
```
Raw numbers: p95 token latency 12.6ms -> 12.0ms, throughput 78k tok/s -> 82k tok/s, peak mem 28GB -> 30.2GB. Worth tracking before we flip selector defaults.:eyes:

aj: Can you drop the micro-bench table here? Need to see batch sizing too. Which batch size & fp mode? Also, which selector rule would prefer FA2 over our fused path?

maria: Batch size = 1 (streaming), fp16. Selector today: prefer fused->flash->paged based on seq-length thresholds + vendor flags. This PR seems to make flash2 more attractive for mid-length (2k-10k) but hurts paged-attn case. Table: seq | fused tput | flash1 | flash2 | peak mem
2k   | 190k      | 185k   | 198k   | 16GB
8k   | 85k       | 78k    | 82k    | 30GB
16k  | 42k       | 38k    | 33k    | 44GB
(rough numbers)

vikram: I ran a quick paged-attn branch (our internal paged-attn w/ KV sharding) on the same env. It drops peak mem by ~35% for 16k+ at cost of ~10-15% throughput for batched workloads. For streaming (bs=1) the latency tail worsens a little. So paged still valuable for on-prem customers with memory caps.

samir: Noted a regression from vLLM recent patch (vllm#42) — deserialization change made KV cache restore slightly slower and bumped tail latencies. Repro steps:
```
python reproduce.py --trace kv-restore --seq 8192
# stack shows: vllm.kv.restore -> copy_kv -> cudaMemcpyAsync slowdown
```
CI flagged two flaky tests in eng-ml perf suite after I rebased. I can open a tracker.

lina: Proposed actions: 1) Add FA2 flag to our kernel matrix and add a canary on Dedicated 1 (non-prod) with traffic shaping for seq 1k/8k/16k. 2) Add an explicit memory-safety fallback: if peak mem > reserved-GB then route to paged-attn. 3) Run end-to-end evals against our quality prompts (some differences seen in FP rounding for flash variants).

aj: Agree with lina. Also want to update selector heuristic so it uses both SLO (p95) and a memory-safety budget. Current selector is single-metric. We should move to a weighted score: score = a*(latency_norm) + b*(mem_norm) + c*(regression_penalty). I'll sketch weights.

maria: I'll file a tracking issue with links to PRs: flash-attn#987, vllm#42, xformers patch set (xformers/pr-314). Assign @vikram to paged-attn + canary run, @samir to vLLM perf regression, @aj to selector changes.

vikram: Started canary run on Dedicated-1. Initial notes: flash2 gives better median but p99 tail for streaming increased slightly when kv cache gets fragmented. Hypothesis: FA2's internal batching path introduces small stalls when caches are warmed. Collecting per-shard timelines.

samir: vLLM patch: reproducer shows 7-12% slower KV load for large caches; looks like an extra host->device memcpy introduced in restore path. I have a minimal fix to avoid the copy; running unit+perf.

ci-bot: build/bench-flash2 #172 finished — status: FAILURE — flaky CUDA OOM in bench matrix (8k, bs=4). See CI link: https://ci.internal/172

lina: OOMs make sense given increased peak mem. For CI we should limit concurrent bench runs or add mem guard in bench harness. Also add a synthetic long-seq test with mem assertions so PRs can't silently increase peaks.

aj: On selector weights: propose a=0.6, b=0.3, c=0.1 for starters. We'll tune after canary results. Also want an emergency fallback policy: if p99 > SLO*1.2 then route 20% traffic to last-known-good kernel.

maria: Action items captured in the tracker. I'll post the issue link when created. TL;DR: FA2 looks promising for mid-length; paged-attn still our best safety valve for very long seqs; vLLM restore regression needs hotfix. We'll gate any global default changes behind canary + perf + quality evals. :rocket:

vikram: Adding perf traces and a sample flamegraph to the issue in ~30m. Will include nvprof/cupti snippets and per-kernel mem alloc timeline.

samir: Patch for vLLM pushed to my fork (fix-kv-copy). Running perf; preliminary: KV restore time down ~9%. Will open PR and link to this thread.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees vendor drop notes (NVIDIA/cuDNN or kernel ABI) ping here. Also keep an eye on xformers PRs — some fused-attn patches are landing that might change our fused path behavior. I'll update the selector RFC after canary results. :white_check_mark:
